questions: Can a bucket be used across multiple wells in a single lowering, or must each lowering be confined to a single well?
If a bucket is partially filled from a well, can it be topped up from another well in the same lowering?
Does the order of lowering buckets matter, e.g., can we optimize by choosing which well to empty first?
Is the bucket lowered exactly once per trip to a well, even if it could extract multiple units in one go due to capacity?
What if capacity is zero? Should we handle it as an error or assume capacity >= 1?
Should the output be an integer, and can we assume the sum of units per well fits in standard integer range?
If a well has zero water, do we still need to lower a bucket into it?
Can we lower multiple buckets into the same well simultaneously, counting as multiple lowerings?
answers: Each lowering is confined to a single well, as the solution sums per-well ceil(units/capacity).
No, because each lowering is per well, so topping up across wells in one lowering is not allowed.
No, order does not matter; the total lowerings is simply the sum over wells of ceil(units/capacity).
Yes, each lowering extracts up to capacity units from a single well, and multiple lowerings per well are needed if units exceed capacity.
The constraints specify 1 <= capacity <= 10, so capacity is at least 1.
Yes, the output is an integer, and the constraints imply sums fit in standard integer range.
No, wells with zero water require zero lowerings, as ceil(0/capacity) = 0.
No, lowerings are sequential per well, and simultaneous lowerings are not considered; each lowering extracts up to capacity units.
